text.p: These are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- The parliament on Wednesday started debating a bill on partial privatisation of Slovenian Ironworks.

- The Governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar said it would be better for the country not to have a budget deficit this year. The government planned a deficit of 27.9 billion tolars ($165.6 million).
- According to unofficial information Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler could resign by the end of this week.
- International petrol company Shell opened its first petrol station in Slovenia on Wednesday. The station was opened in Jesenice, a town northwest of Ljubljana.
- The soccer team of Maribor made it to the second round of European Cup qualifications, while Nova Gorica managed to get to the second preliminary round of UEFA Cup.
- State-owned mobile phone network operator Mobitel said it expected the number of GSM phone users to jump to 200,000 by the year 2000 from current 20,000.
- Textile firm Bombazna Predilnica in Tkalnica from Trzic may go into bankruptcy due to financial problems that have been dragging on for years.

- The opposition parties demanded a special parliamentary session where the parliament would debate the government's responsibility for Slovenia not being included in the first round of NATO expansion.
- About 70,000 people are expected to visit a Micheal Jackson concert in Ljubljana on August 8, the organiser of the concert said.
